frozen_candidate_root_contribution: wqt = the fixing/designation of a determinate, appointed temporal boundary — a set point OR a bounded term at/for which something occurs. It supplies the appointedness/fixedness of a time, not time-as-flow or duration-as-such, not the event/entity itself, and not place.

internal_discovery.candidate_root_contribution: wqt = the fixing/designation of a determinate, appointed temporal boundary — a set point OR a bounded term at/for which something occurs. It supplies the appointedness/fixedness of a time, not time-as-flow or duration-as-such, not the event/entity itself, and not place.
internal_discovery.plain_explanation: Across all 13 occurrences the root marks a time that has been fixed or appointed, never generic elapsing time. The base noun waqt is a determinate moment (the 'known time' of respite in 15:38=38:81; the hidden-but-fixed time of the Hour in 7:187). The mif'al noun miqat is an appointed time/term (the Day of Decision in 44:40/78:17; the gathering of a known day in 26:38/56:50; Moses's appointment in 7:143/7:155; a term 'completed at forty nights' in 7:142). The plural mawaqit are calendrical time-markers (2:189, the crescents). The participle mawqut is prayer 'made time-fixed' (4:103). The sole verb, Form II passive uqqitat (77:11), is 'the messengers are assigned their appointed time.' The common core is demarcation/appointment of a time; whether that time is a point or a span, a one-off decree or a recurring marker, is supplied by context, not by the root.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: wqt does NOT entail: (1) time as continuum/flow/duration or an age/epoch — every occurrence is delimited/appointed; (2) the event or content itself — it frames yawm, al-sa'ah (7:187 distinguishes the Hour from li-waqtiha), al-salah, and the Day of Decision, but does not name them; (3) knownness/disclosure — the 'known' comes from the added modifier al-ma'lum (15:38/38:81) or ma'lum (26:38/56:50), while 7:187 makes the waqt explicitly hidden to all but God; (4) punctuality only — 7:142 is a bounded span of forty nights that reaches completion; (5) place/spatial locus — the mif'al form miqat stays temporal throughout (2:189 = lunar phases; 7:142 = forty nights). The count/quantity of a span (forty nights, seventy men) is carried by other words, not by wqt.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: 7:142:8:1 — «فَتَمَّ مِيقَٰتُ رَبِّهِۦٓ أَرْبَعِينَ لَيْلَةً». Because the miqat is 'completed' (tamma) and quantified as forty nights, it behaves as a bounded term/duration rather than a punctual instant. This blocks the narrower gloss 'fixed appointed moment/deadline' and forces the nucleus to be stated as 'fixed point OR bounded term,' reducing its discriminating sharpness. It refines the account rather than breaking it.
internal_discovery.strongest_competitor: 'wqt = generic time (a bare temporal noun; fixedness supplied only by context).' Attractive because waqt is a plausible word for 'time.' Rejected on Quran-internal grounds: the corpus never once uses wqt for time-as-flow, and the fixing is carried internally by the derived morphology (mif'al instrument-noun miqat/mawaqit, passive participle mawqut, Form-II uqqitat) and by the recurrent pairing with al-ma'lum/ma'lum. A secondary competitor — 'miqat is a lexicalized nominal class distinct from base waqt, possibly with a spatial rendezvous sense' — is defeated by the shared «yawm…ma'lum» collocation across the base noun (15:38/38:81) and the mif'al noun (26:38/56:50), and by the fact that no spatial reading is ever attested (2:189 = crescents; 7:142 = forty nights).
internal_discovery.competing_hypothesis: 'wqt = generic time (a bare temporal noun; fixedness supplied only by context).' Attractive because waqt is a plausible word for 'time.' Rejected on Quran-internal grounds: the corpus never once uses wqt for time-as-flow, and the fixing is carried internally by the derived morphology (mif'al instrument-noun miqat/mawaqit, passive participle mawqut, Form-II uqqitat) and by the recurrent pairing with al-ma'lum/ma'lum. A secondary competitor — 'miqat is a lexicalized nominal class distinct from base waqt, possibly with a spatial rendezvous sense' — is defeated by the shared «yawm…ma'lum» collocation across the base noun (15:38/38:81) and the mif'al noun (26:38/56:50), and by the fact that no spatial reading is ever attested (2:189 = crescents; 7:142 = forty nights).
internal_discovery.rationale: All three lenses agree the nucleus — fixing/designation of a determinate appointed time — governs every one of the 13 occurrences with no contradicting occurrence, so the result is PREFERRED and not UNRESOLVED: the derivational family is Quran-internally bridged (shared «yawm…ma'lum» frame across base and mif'al forms; the mif'al = instrument/appointed-time by which time is fixed; mawqut = 'made-time-fixed'; uqqitat = 'to have a time fixed'). This rules out forcing a multi-class or homonym split. The grade is capped at MODERATE / REPRESENTATIVE (DERIVATIONAL_FAMILY) rather than STRONG / UNIVERSAL because the adversarial lens exposes real limits on distinctive breadth: (a) 12/13 occurrences are nominal or adjectival, and the entire dynamic/verbal 'to appoint a time' sense rests on a single hapax verb (77:11 uqqitat), so the active semantics is not independently corroborated; (b) the apparent breadth is inflated by formulaic repetition — al-waqt al-ma'lum (x2 identical), li-miqatina (x2 identical), miqati yawmin ma'lumin (x2 near-identical), yawm al-fasl = miqat (x2) — leaving roughly 8 effectively independent contexts; (c) unifying all 13 requires stating the nucleus at an abstraction ('determinacy/fixedness of time') broad enough to absorb point/term and appointment/marker/recurrence flavors, so it is non-vacuous but not sharply discriminating in the way STRONG demands. There is nonetheless NO coherent resistant sub-class: the two boundary occurrences (7:142 bounded term; 2:189 recurring calendrical marker) and the hapax verb all bridge to the nucleus, which is why the honest verdict is MODERATE — neither inflated to STRONG nor deflated to RESISTANT/UNRESOLVED.

independent_verification: Cross-lens: Analysts A and B independently derived the same nucleus and graded STRONG; adversary C independently confirmed no contradicting occurrence but argued the nominal-dominant, formulaic, hapax-anchored, abstraction-leaning evidence caps below STRONG. The aggregator adopts C's calibrated ceiling.
candidate_root_contribution: wqt = the fixing/designation of a determinate, appointed temporal boundary — a set point OR a bounded term at/for which something occurs. It supplies the appointedness/fixedness of a time, not time-as-flow or duration-as-such, not the event/entity itself, and not place.

layer_attribution.occurrence_evidence: 13/13 confirmed occurrences read with QAC morphology: base noun waqt x3 (15:38:3:2, 38:81:3:2, 7:187:13:2), mif'al singular miqat x7 (26:38, 44:40, 56:50, 78:17, 7:142, 7:143, 7:155), mif'al plural mawaqit x1 (2:189), passive participle mawqut x1 (4:103), Form-II passive verb uqqitat x1 (77:11).
layer_attribution.derivation: The root is realized across a derivational family unified by one nucleus: base noun = the fixed time; mif'al noun miqat/mawaqit = the appointed-time/instrument by which time is fixed; passive participle mawqut = 'made-time-fixed' (patient of the factitive Form II waqqata); Form-II passive uqqitat = 'to have a time fixed/assigned.' The factitive Form-II morphology encodes appointing/fixing, not merely 'time.'
layer_attribution.lexical_class: miqat (with its plural mawaqit) is a partly lexicalized mif'al nominal dominating 8/13 tokens; it is Quran-internally bridged to the base noun by the shared «yawm…ma'lum» frame, so it is a paradigmatic realization of the root contribution rather than a resistant separate class — but its lexicalized, formulaic dominance is a principal reason the grade is capped at MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE.
layer_attribution.contextual_relation: Contextual notions — gathering/meeting (jumi'a, majmu'un, ja'a), decision (yawm al-fasl), respite (Iblis), Moses's tryst, Hajj scheduling, and the count of a span (forty nights, seventy men) — are supplied by neighbouring lexemes, NOT by wqt. The root contributes only the fixed-time framing; these narrative meanings must not be absorbed into the root claim.
layer_attribution.reconciliation: Lenses A and B (STRONG/UNIVERSAL) and adversary C (MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE) converge on the same nucleus and on the absence of any contradicting occurrence; they diverge only on grade. Reconciled to MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE (DERIVATIONAL_FAMILY): the unity is real and uncontradicted (so PREFERRED, not UNRESOLVED), but nominal-dominance, formulaic inflation, a single hapax verbal anchor, and an abstraction-leaning nucleus preclude STRONG.
layer_attribution.unresolved_resistance: No genuine resistant sub-class and no persisted resistance: the two boundary occurrences (7:142 bounded term; 2:189 recurring calendrical marker) and the hapax verb (77:11) all bridge to the nucleus. Residual, non-fatal limits are the thin verbal corroboration (one hapax) and the mild calendrical scope-stretch of 2:189, recorded as adversarial boundaries rather than resistance.

hard_cases.reason: miqat here is a bounded term/duration ('completed at forty nights'), not a punctual instant, blocking the narrower 'fixed moment/deadline' formulation and reducing the nucleus's discriminating sharpness.

evidence_basis.statement: 7:142:8:1 «فَتَمَّ مِيقَٰتُ رَبِّهِۦٓ أَرْبَعِينَ لَيْلَةً» — the miqat is completed (tamma) and quantified as forty nights, forcing the nucleus to widen from 'fixed point' to 'fixed point or bounded term.'

hard_cases.reason: mawaqit are periodic calendrical instruments for mundane human/Hajj reckoning, the widest scope-stretch away from the dominant single-divine-appointment sense; it marks the outer boundary of the nucleus.

evidence_basis.statement: 2:189:6:1 «هِىَ مَوَٰقِيتُ لِلنَّاسِ وَٱلْحَجِّ» — recurring calendrical markers for people and Hajj, a recurring-marker flavor distinct from the one-off appointment, confirming the mif'al = instruments for fixing time rather than a single eschatological point.

hard_cases.reason: The sole finite verb and a hapax; the entire dynamic/verbal 'to appoint a time' sense of the root rests on this single datum, read via morphology plus context rather than any internal verbal parallel.

evidence_basis.statement: 77:11:3:1 «وَإِذَا ٱلرُّسُلُ أُقِّتَتْ» — a Form-II passive hapax verb; the active/dynamic semantics is not independently corroborated, so the verbal anchor is a singleton that caps distinctive breadth.

hard_case_representation.rationale: No occurrence attains final-RESISTANT disposition — the nucleus is uncontradicted across all 13. The hard cases are evidence-derived adversarial boundaries (7:142 bounded term; 2:189 recurring calendrical marker) and a structural atypicality (77:11 hapax verb) that constrain the calibrated width and cap the grade at MODERATE, not resistant seams. Each hard case's statement also appears as strongest_counterexample (7:142) or in its cluster note (2:189 in C3; 77:11 in C5).

rejection_condition.challenging_finding: An occurrence of wqt used for undifferentiated flowing time, a lifespan/age/epoch, or a mere duration WITHOUT any appointed/fixed boundary — i.e., the root supplying 'time-as-such' rather than a set/appointed time.
rejection_condition.search_location: Re-examine every base-noun waqt (15:38:3:2, 38:81:3:2, 7:187:13:2) and any miqat that lacks an anchoring event/terminus, checking whether the fixedness is carried by wqt or only by surrounding words (yawm, ma'lum, tamma, ruslu).
rejection_condition.verification_method: Strip each occurrence of its external qualifiers (al-ma'lum, yawm, arba'in laylah, li-...) and test whether a determinate/appointed reading survives on wqt alone; compare against the contrastive frames al-sa'ah (7:187) and yawm (15:38, 26:38, 44:40, 78:17).
rejection_condition.confounder_control: Distinguish root-borne fixedness from modifier-borne knownness (al-ma'lum) and from context-borne event content (jumi'a/majmu'un, yawm al-fasl); do not credit the root with meanings supplied by adjacent lexemes or by the count words (forty nights, seventy men).
rejection_condition.failure_consequence: If a genuine flowing-time / duration-as-such use is found that resists the appointed-boundary nucleus, downgrade from MODERATE and either narrow to a LEXICALIZED_CLASS around miqat or move to UNRESOLVED_CLASS_ONLY if the base noun and mif'al noun no longer share one bridge.

reopen_conditions: If a second independent Form-II or other finite verb of wqt is identified in the corpus, re-test whether the dynamic 'to appoint a time' sense (now resting solely on the hapax 77:11 uqqitat) is corroborated, which could lift the grade toward STRONG.

If a base-noun waqt or miqat is found functioning as a spatial locus/meeting-PLACE (rather than temporally, as in 2:189 crescents and 7:142 forty nights), reopen the negative boundary 'not place' and reconsider whether miqat is a partially lexicalized class distinct from base waqt.

If any wqt occurrence is read as generic flowing time or duration-as-such without an appointed boundary, reopen the core nucleus and the base-vs-mif'al bridge (currently welded by the «yawm…ma'lum» collocation shared across 15:38/38:81 and 26:38/56:50).

falsification_evidence.status_rationale: No occurrence contradicts the appointed-time-boundary nucleus, so the adversarial attempt returns SUPPORTED and neither RESISTANT nor UNRESOLVED is warranted. A full PASS is NOT claimed (hence NOT_RUN): distinctiveness_ok is set false because the nucleus rests on an abstraction ('determinacy/fixedness of time') that is non-vacuous but not sharply discriminating, breadth is inflated by formulaic repetition (~8 independent contexts among 13), 12/13 tokens are nominal/adjectival, and the sole verbal anchor is a hapax (77:11). These reservations cap the grade at MODERATE rather than certifying a clean adversarial PASS.
